description: Core concepts of communication systems, network topologies, LAN/MAN/WAN types, Huawei network devices (switches, routers, firewalls, WLAN), modular vs. fixed chassis architecture, and packet encapsulation flow.

lessons.title: Communication & Tech Evolution
lessons.summary: Learn the three core elements of a communication system and trace communication from ancient beacons to 5G/6G and IoE.

lessons.title: Networks & Topologies
lessons.summary: Understand network communication examples, datacom network components, and compare bus, star, ring, tree, and mesh topologies.

lessons.title: LAN, MAN, WAN & Enterprise
lessons.summary: Classify networks by geographical coverage (LAN, MAN, WAN) and by operation entity (Enterprise vs. Carrier networks).

lessons.title: Core Network Devices
lessons.summary: Master the roles of switches (MAC forwarding), routers (IP path selection), firewalls (egress security), and WLAN devices (Fat/Fit/Cloud APs & WAC).

lessons.title: Huawei Hardware & Data Flow
lessons.summary: Explore modular (MPU/SFU/LPU) vs. fixed chassis hardware, then trace packet encapsulation from sender to receiver using the postal analogy.

lessons.title: Engineering, Certification & Quiz
lessons.summary: Review network engineering competencies, the Huawei Datacom certification track (HCIA -> HCIP -> HCIE), and pass the official Huawei quiz.

challenge.prompt: Arrange these communication milestones in chronological order from oldest to newest (Slide 6):
items: Visual and auditory signals (Beacon fires, ~3000 BCE)
challenge.explanation: Communication progressed from Ancient times (~3000 BCE beacons) -> Electrical era (1830s telegraph) -> Information era (1960s–1970s ARPANET) -> IoE era (late 2010s 5G and beyond).

challenge.prompt: Match each network topology to its defining Huawei textbook characteristic (Slide 10):

pairs.right: Failure of the shared bus affects the entire network; insecure
Easy to add nodes & monitor, but central node is a single point of failure
Uses fewer cables, but adding a node requires breaking the ring
Highest reliability & efficiency, but costly and hard to scale

challenge.explanation: Real-world networks combine topologies to balance cost, performance, and reliability. Star is easy to expand; Full-mesh maximizes redundancy at high port/cable cost.

challenge.prompt: Which network type spans tens to thousands of kilometers to interconnect distant LANs or MANs using technologies such as PPP, MPLS, and SRv6?
challenge.explanation: A WAN covers tens to thousands of kilometers across cities or countries and relies on technologies like PPP, MPLS, and SRv6 (Slide 12).

challenge.prompt: Complete the core forwarding comparison between switches and routers (Slides 18–19):
challenge.template: A switch forwards data frames on a LAN using the destination [0] address, whereas a router selects paths for data packets using the destination [1] address.
challenge.explanation: Switches identify the destination MAC address inside data frames on a LAN; routers examine the destination IP address in data packets to select the next hop.

challenge.prompt: Which Huawei AP working mode is managed centrally by a Wireless Access Controller (WAC) and suits midsize-to-large enterprises?
challenge.explanation: A Fit AP must work together with a WAC for unified management and configuration, making it ideal for midsize and large enterprises. Fat APs work independently for home use (Slide 21).

challenge.prompt: Match each modular Huawei CloudEngine S12700H-8 board to its hardware role (Slides 24 & 26):

pairs.right: Mandatory board that controls, manages, and monitors the system
Mandatory switch fabric that forwards traffic between all LPUs
Optional board that processes data packets and manages port traffic
Optional board that monitors ambient temperature and environment

challenge.explanation: In a modular chassis, MPU (control) and SFU (switching fabric) are mandatory; LPUs provide line interfaces and communicate through the SFUs.

challenge.prompt: Which TWO statements accurately describe data encapsulation and common terms? (Slides 28–29)
options: Encapsulation adds a header (and optionally a trailer) to a data payload
A gateway is a specific physical hardware box model with no routing function
Decapsulation removes the header and trailer to recover the data payload
Every network packet is required to include a trailer
challenge.explanation: Encapsulation wraps a payload with a header/trailer, and decapsulation strips them off. Note that Huawei explicitly points out many packets do not have a trailer, and 'gateway' is named by its deployment location/function rather than a single device type.

challenge.prompt: Order the Huawei Datacom Certification levels from foundational to expert (Slides 35–36):
challenge.explanation: Huawei's hierarchical certification path grows from Associate (HCIA) -> Professional (HCIP) -> Expert (HCIE).
